items.title: A separable algebraic base change with separably closed residue fields, in which solutions descend, exists for any extension of discrete valuation rings
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra)

items.difficulty_reason: The lemma asserts that for any extension A -> B of discrete valuation rings there is a commutative square of such extensions with three properties: the induced fraction field extensions K'/K and L'/L are separable algebraic; the residue fields of A' and B' are separable algebraic closures of those of A and B; and if a solution, weak solution or separable solution exists for A' -> B' then one exists for A -> B (source lines 34554-34574). The proof constructs the square and then proves the descent. Construction: the colimit-finite-etale lemma gives a filtered colimit A' of finite etale extensions of A whose residue field is a separable algebraic closure of that of A, and taking B' to be a strict henselization of B gives the square with parts (1) and (2) clear (proof lines 34577-34590). The substantive part is the descent: given a (weak) solution K'_1/K' for A' -> B', the proof uses that A' is a colimit to find a finite etale extension A subset A'_1 and a finite extension K_1 of its fraction field F with K'_1 = K' tensor_F K_1; since A subset A'_1 is finite etale and B' is strictly henselian, B' tensor_A A'_1 is a finite product of rings isomorphic to B', so that L' tensor_K K_1 = L' tensor_K F tensor_F K_1 is a finite product of rings isomorphic to L' tensor_{K'} K'_1; hence K_1/K is a (weak) solution for A -> B', and therefore also one for A -> B by the solutions-go-down lemma (proof lines 34593-34605). The non-routine content is the combination of the colimit description of A' with the strict henselianness of B' to make the tensor products split into copies of B'.
